Navigating Autism & Anxiety

Anxiety is highly common among autistic individuals. It is often triggered by sensory overload, the pressure to mask social differences, and sudden changes in routines. At eMbrace, we offer neuro-affirming therapy that helps clients manage anxiety while respecting their unique neurology.

Anxiety Triggers & Presentations

  • Sensory Load: Crowded, noisy, or bright spaces that overstimulate the nervous system, causing physical anxiety.
  • Social Pressures: Fear of social mistakes or the exhaustion of masking traits in public.
  • Unpredictable Schedules: Sudden changes in routines that increase cognitive load and stress.
  • Interoception Differences: Difficulty identifying physical signs of anxiety (like heart rate) until it feels overwhelming.

Cognitive & Regulation Therapy

We combine CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) adapted for autism, sensory regulation, and somatic calming strategies. We focus on identifying early triggers and developing personalized sensory kits.

Frequently Asked Questions

The autistic nervous system is highly sensitive to sensory inputs and changes. Processing a neurotypical-designed world requires constant cognitive effort, which can lead to high baseline anxiety.

We make CBT more visual and concrete. We focus on physical sensory regulation and environmental changes rather than only trying to change thought patterns.

Wondering whether an assessment is actually needed?

Our early-signs screener profiles four behaviour clusters separately — attention, impulsivity, social communication, and routines and sensory needs — and weighs how much daily life is affected. You get a straight answer on whether to book, plus a free guide to what an assessment involves and a school accommodations letter template.
